_what: Phrases a speech-to-text model got wrong, which must never reach a caption card.
_why: Six of these were found by hand in one 26-minute recording, after the cards were already written. A card carrying a mishearing is burned in: it cannot be fixed after rendering. caption_check.py reads this file by default.
_how: Each entry is a phrase the transcriber produced, the phrase that was actually said, and where it was found. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries, so 'couch' does not fire inside 'couching'. Phrases, not bare words: 'piece' is a real word, 'world piece' is not.
_yours: THIS IS A STARTING LIST, NOT YOUR LIST. Every one of these came from one speaker's recording. Add your own the first time you read a transcript: your name, your product names, the jargon of your field, the two or three words you say in a way the model mishears. The single highest value row is your own name, because a card that misspells the speaker is the one a viewer notices.
_name_row: Replace the NAME row below with your own. The entry is here as the shape to copy, and because a misheard name is the commonest and most visible defect of the lot.
